sections.heading: First Person Boxing on Roblox: Official Game & Fast Facts
paragraphs: The correct First Person Boxing experience is published by Can You Box? on Roblox. Use the official game link above, rather than similarly titled downloads or other boxing games. The official Place ID is 132956556682909; the separate Universe ID is not a substitute for a playable Place link.

The Roblox description identifies the main appeal directly: see each attack from a first-person viewpoint, slip a punch, answer with a counter, choose a guard for the threatened area, and avoid becoming exhausted. That is a better introduction than an invented tier list or unverified win-rate chart.

Game identity and supported-platform details were checked against the public Roblox listing on October 18, 2026. Player counts move quickly, so this guide deliberately does not publish a supposedly live online-player figure.

subsections.heading: Which Roblox Experience Is the Correct One?
paragraphs: Look for the experience named First Person Boxing and the creator Can You Box?. The approved link points to Roblox Place 132956556682909. Untitled Boxing Game and First-Person Boxing: Circuit Clash are different experiences; their codes and controls must not be mixed with this game.

subsections.heading: Can You Play on PC, Mobile and Console?
paragraphs: Yes: the official First Person Boxing description explicitly lists PC, Mobile and Console. That statement confirms the offered platforms, not identical keyboard, touch and controller bindings. Consult the controls guide for a device-specific reference and how to inspect the current in-game prompts.

sections.heading: What You Do in First Person Boxing
paragraphs: A fight is not simply a race to press attack. The official description highlights a sequence of decisions: judge an incoming strike, defend the right target or move out of the punch line, respond with a counter when an opening appears, then recover your position.

The first-person camera makes reading distance important. Try to keep your opponent in view and make one deliberate decision per exchange before adding faster attacks. This is practice advice, not a claim about hidden damage multipliers or exact frame timings.

subsections.heading: Offense, Defense and Stamina
paragraphs: Offense means choosing when to throw. Defense includes two guard targets—head and body—and a slip to evade a strike. Stamina is a limited resource; the official listing warns that tired fighters slow down. If your movement feels less responsive after repeated actions, create distance rather than assuming that a longer button sequence is always better.

subsections.heading: AI Practice Versus Fighting Other Players
paragraphs: The Roblox description explicitly offers AI practice alongside fighting players. AI is a useful place to rehearse a repeatable defense sequence without relying on an opponent to cooperate. Actual PvP opponents change their rhythm, so a drill that works against AI remains a starting point rather than a guaranteed winning move.

sections.heading: Beginner Path: Your First AI Practice Round
paragraphs: Open the official Roblox experience and identify the movement, attack, defense and camera prompts for your device before jumping into a live match. A useful first round is not about winning instantly. It is about learning what the screen tells you when you are about to be hit.

For the first few exchanges, focus on the opponent's movement and the visible stamina state. Practice a guard without rushing to attack, then attempt one deliberate slip. Only after those inputs are familiar should you try to place a short counter.

Repeat the sequence against AI until you can reliably describe what happened: which punch you saw, which defense you chose, whether your response connected, and whether you still had stamina to leave safely.

subsections.heading: Common First-Match Mistakes
paragraphs: Do not import keybinds, reward codes or style names from another Roblox boxing game. Do not assume every player-facing input on desktop will be available as the same key on mobile or console. When a code or key behaves differently after an update, rely on the current game interface rather than a copied old list.

subsections.heading: A Repeatable Five-Minute Routine
paragraphs: Spend the first minute checking inputs; the second keeping the opponent centered; the third alternating guard choices; the fourth testing slips on clearly visible attacks; and the fifth performing one measured counter before resetting. These durations are suggested training structure, not official game rules.

faq: Is First Person Boxing a Roblox game?
Yes. First Person Boxing is a Roblox experience by Can You Box?. Follow the official Roblox game link on this page.
Where can I play First Person Boxing?
Use the original Roblox experience at Place ID 132956556682909. This guide does not run the game in your browser.
Does First Person Boxing support mobile and console?
The official Roblox description lists PC, Mobile and Console. Controls differ by device.
Does First Person Boxing have codes?
Dated third-party sources report redeemable codes. Read our codes page for individual strings and their unverified status; we do not claim in-game redemptions.
How do I slip and counter?
Read the opponent's attack, use a slip or appropriate guard, throw a measured response when an opening appears, and reset. The detailed drill is in our Slip & Counter Guide.
Is this the same as Untitled Boxing Game?
No. Untitled Boxing Game is a separate Roblox experience; its codes and style lists are not for First Person Boxing.
